_comment: Curated cluster -> role-family map for the trends ledger (ADR-0040). Keys on centroid_version: the cluster ids are meaningless against any other fit, so a refit re-curates this file. Every cluster of the fit must appear exactly once here or in non_tech - headstart.roles.load_families refuses to load otherwise, because an unmapped cluster would silently vanish from every chart. Cluster contents are in the fit's manifest.json (label + top_titles); the counts below are count_at_fit, kept as a sanity anchor for review.

families.name: software-engineering
families.label: Software Engineering (general)
families.note: The catch-all for backend/frontend/fullstack/platform SWE titles that k-means split by seniority and phrasing rather than by domain. 71 is a location-boilerplate cluster ('Remote, Latin America') holding genuinely mixed tech roles; 48 is one Windows/Desktop posting replicated across ~30 cities.

families.name: web-development
families.label: Web & .NET Development
families.note: Full Stack / .Net / Web / ServiceNow developer titles.

families.name: ai-ml
families.label: AI / Machine Learning
families.note: 51 is the startup-shaped cluster (Forward Deployed / GTM / Product Engineer alongside AI Engineer).

families.name: hardware-embedded
families.label: Hardware, Firmware & Silicon
families.note: Firmware, ASIC/design verification, physical design. 36 mixes chip design with fab equipment maintenance.

families.name: product-management
families.label: Product & Technical Program Management
families.note: Mixed: Product Manager alongside founder/CTO and lead-scientist titles.

families.name: it-operations
families.label: IT & Data Centre Operations
families.note: Sysadmin/DBA plus data-centre technicians — infrastructure operations, not software authoring.

non_tech._comment: Excluded from the chart, counted into one (non-tech, all) ledger row per run as an ADR-0017 filter-health series. These are what the recall-biased tech filter lets through, and the clustering concentrates them.
